extracted.subtask_description: A professional code describing core values and conduct provisions for PRSA members and public relations practitioners, covering values (advocacy, honesty, expertise, independence, loyalty, fairness) and specific provisions (free flow of information, competition, disclosure, safeguarding confidences, conflicts of interest, enhancing the profession).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: We serve the public interest by acting as responsible advocates for those we represent. We provide a voice in the marketplace of ideas, facts, and viewpoints to aid informed public debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a core professional value, advocacy means representing clients' interests responsibly while contributing to informed public debate. No additional examples are provided under this heading on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: We adhere to the highest standards of accuracy and truth in advancing the interests of those we represent and in communicating with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honesty requires accuracy and truthfulness in all communications on behalf of those represented; see related provisions (e.g., Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information) for concrete guidelines and examples of improper conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: We acquire and responsibly use specialized knowledge and experience. We advance the profession through continued professional development, research, and education. We build mutual understanding, credibility, and relationships among a wide array of institutions and audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should pursue continuing professional development, apply specialized knowledge responsibly, and promote the profession through research and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide objective counsel to those we represent. We are accountable for our actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence requires offering objective counsel and taking responsibility for professional actions; this value connects to conflicts-of-interest guidance requiring disclosure and avoidance of compromising circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: We are faithful to those we represent, while honoring our obligation to serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loyalty balances faithfulness to clients or employers with the obligation to the public interest; members must avoid actions that unduly prioritize personal or other interests over clients' or the public's welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: We deal fairly with clients, employers, competitors, peers, vendors, the media, and the general public. We respect all opinions and support the right of free expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fairness implies ethical hiring and competitive practices, respect for intellectual property and free expression, and refraining from spreading malicious or unfounded rumors (see Competition examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Free Flow of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle Protecting and advancing the free flow of accurate and truthful information is essential to serving the public interest and contributing to informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: To maintain the integrity of relationships with the media, government officials, and the public; To aid informed decision-making. Guidelines: Preserve the integrity of the process of communication; Be honest and accurate in all communications; Act promptly to correct erroneous communications for which the practitioner is responsible; Preserve the free flow of unprejudiced information when giving or receiving gifts by ensuring that gifts are nominal, legal, and infrequent. Examples of Improper Conduct: giving expensive products to influence coverage; entertaining government officials beyond legal limits or in violation of reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle Promoting healthy and fair competition among professionals preserves an ethical climate while fostering a robust business environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: To promote respect and fair competition among public relations professionals; To serve the public interest by providing the widest choice of practitioner options. Guidelines: Follow ethical hiring practices designed to respect free and open competition without deliberately undermining a competitor; Preserve intellectual property rights in the marketplace. Examples of Improper Conduct: sharing helpful information with a competing firm bidding for the same business; spreading malicious and unfounded rumors about a competitor to recruit people and business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle Open communication fosters informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: To build trust with the public by revealing all information needed for responsible decision making. Guidelines: Be honest and accurate in all communications; Act promptly to correct erroneous communications for which the member is responsible; Investigate the truthfulness and accuracy of information released on behalf of those represented; Reveal the sponsors for causes and interests represented; Disclose financial interest (such as stock ownership) in a client’s organization; Avoid deceptive practices. Examples of Improper Conduct: creating front groups for undisclosed interests; lying by omission about financial information; failing to correct inaccurate information; employing people to pose as volunteers in 'grass roots' campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Confidences
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle Client trust requires appropriate protection of confidential and private information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: To protect the privacy rights of clients, organizations, and individuals by safeguarding confidential information. Guidelines: Safeguard the confidences and privacy rights of present, former, and prospective clients and employees; Protect privileged, confidential, or insider information gained from a client or organization; Immediately advise an appropriate authority if a member discovers that confidential information is being divulged by an employee of a client company or organization. Examples of Improper Conduct: changing jobs and using confidential information to the detriment of a former employer; intentionally leaking proprietary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle Avoiding real, potential or perceived conflicts of interest builds the trust of clients, employers, and the publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: To earn trust and mutual respect with clients or employers; To build trust with the public by avoiding or ending situations that put one’s personal or professional interests in conflict with society’s interests. Guidelines: Act in the best interests of the client or employer, even subordinating the member’s personal interests; Avoid actions and circumstances that may appear to compromise good business judgment or create a conflict between personal and professional interests; Disclose promptly any existing or potential conflict of interest to affected clients or organizations; Encourage clients and customers to determine if a conflict exists after notifying all affected parties. Examples of Improper Conduct: failing to disclose a strong financial interest in a client's chief competitor; representing a competitor or conflicting interest without informing a prospective client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing the Profession
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle Public relations professionals work constantly to strengthen the public’s trust in the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: To build respect and credibility with the public for the profession of public relations; To improve, adapt and expand professional practices. Guidelines: Acknowledge an obligation to protect and enhance the profession; Keep informed and educated about practices in the profession to ensure ethical conduct; Actively pursue personal professional development; Decline representation of clients or organizations that urge or require actions contrary to this Code; Accurately define what public relations activities can accomplish; Counsel subordinates in proper ethical decision making; Require that subordinates adhere to the ethical requirements of the Code; Report practices that fail to comply with the Code, whether committed by PRSA members or not, to the appropriate authority. Examples of Improper Conduct: declaring a product safe without disclosing contrary evidence; assigning questionable client work to a non-member to avoid ethical obligations.
